subject: Partial availability Dec 6 — peering overlap & apportionment
messages:
From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@fidelitycloud.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fidelitycloud.com
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 11:12:00 +0000
Subject: Partial availability Dec 6 — request for SLA assessment

Hi Rohan,

We observed a partial degradation against the Redwood API for a subset of our traffic on Dec 6 between ~03:08–03:26 UTC (our edge probes). Some requests returned 503s and others experienced latency spikes up to 1.8s. We've attached a small sample (edge-probes.csv) with our probe timestamps and HTTP traces.

We saw a spike that aligns with a BGP flap reported by our peering provider and would like Redwood to confirm whether this should be considered a third-party outage (and therefore excluded from uptime calculations) or if it falls under Redwood's partial availability window.

Request: please confirm the timeline you see on your side and a proposed apportionment or credit if applicable. We need this for our internal incident review and for the renewal conversation next quarter.

Attachments: edge-probes.csv

Thanks,
Alyssa Turner
SRE, FidelityCloud
alyssa@fidelitycloud.com

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@fidelitycloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 13:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Partial availability Dec 6 — request for SLA assessment

Thanks Alyssa — appreciate the sample traces. We're actively looking into this. Quick notes from our side:

- We had a scheduled maintenance action in us-west-2 on Dec 6 (03:00–03:40 UTC) to rotate an egress router. The maintenance manifest (internal) is attached for reference.
- Our telemetry shows a period of elevated error-rate and slow tails from 03:10–03:22 UTC on the path servicing a subset of probes. Outside of that range we don't see sustained failures.

Before we propose apportionment, can you confirm whether the timestamps in your CSV are source-probe time (they appear to be) and include the raw TCP traces if possible. Also: do you have the NetPath contact log from your upstream (Jacob from NetPath.io) that references the BGP activity? If you can share that we can compare BGP peer state transitions with our egress maintenance window.

Cc'ing Marissa (SRE lead) and Naomi (Customer Success) so we can align on apportionment methodology and credits if warranted. We'll aim to respond with a proposed split by EOD.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Account Lead, Reliability Escalations
Redwood Inference
rohan_mehta@redwood.com

Attachment: maintenance_manifest.pdf

From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@fidelitycloud.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fidelitycloud.com, Jacob Lin <jacob@netpath.io>
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 14:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Partial availability Dec 6 — request for SLA assessment

Hi Rohan — thanks for the quick reply.

I've uploaded the full probe dump and the NetPath BGP logs; pulling a subset here. The timestamps in edge-probes.csv are our active synthetic probes (source UTC). NetPath's log shows a peer flap at 03:11:24 UTC that impacted our egress to a subset of customers for roughly 5–7 minutes (netpath-bgp-log.txt attached). We're pushing NetPath on a post-mortem; Jacob, can you confirm the flap timing?

We agree your maintenance window overlaps, but from our POV the BGP flap looks like the initiating event and we believe that should qualify as a third-party exclusion. We'd prefer Redwood attribute the initial impact to the upstream provider and only apply a narrow window (if any) of Redwood responsibility.

Attachments: edge-probes.csv, netpath-bgp-log.txt

Thanks,
Alyssa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@fidelitycloud.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 15:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Partial availability Dec 6 — request for SLA assessment

Hi all — looping in with our initial apportionment analysis so we're transparent about our method. We're proposing a conservative split based on timeline correlation and control-plane signals:

- Redwood telemetry: partial degradation window 03:10:00–03:22:00 UTC (elevated 5xxs and increased tail latency).
- NetPath reported BGP flap at 03:11:24 UTC (Alyssa's attachment).

Proposal: apportion responsibility by time overlap and signal origin. Because our maintenance change began earlier and completed at 03:40 UTC, but the observable spike aligns with an external peer flap, propose 40% Redwood / 60% third-party for the 03:11–03:18 UTC net impact. For the tail window 03:18–03:22 UTC (post-flap stabilization) we propose 70% Redwood responsibility due to retransmits and queueing visible on our egress routers.

Attached is a short calc workbook and our probe sampling method (apportionment_calc.xlsx). If FidelityCloud can provide packet captures from a probe that saw the initial SYN retransmit we can tighten the split further.

We intend to use an apportionment approach rather than an all-or-nothing exclusion because the signal chain shows both events contributing. If you'd like to escalate to a formal SLA committee review we'll schedule a 30-minute alignment call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: apportionment_calc.xlsx

From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@fidelitycloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fidelitycloud.com, Jacob Lin <jacob@netpath.io>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Partial availability Dec 6 — request for SLA assessment

Marissa — thanks for the breakdown. We appreciate the attempt to be granular, but FidelityCloud's position is that the initiating root cause was the third-party BGP flap. We cannot accept a split that assigns >25% responsibility to Redwood for the initial impact window. Our procurement/finance team will need a clear exclusion to support any denial of credit.

We'd like to:
- Escalate this to an SLA committee review (please propose times this week).
- Request the raw egress packet captures for the impacted flow (SYN/ACK retransmit windows) and any router queueing counters for the 03:08–03:26 UTC range.
- Confirm what credit would look like under both the split and full-exclusion models so we can take to our procurement team.

If we can't reach an agreement we will escalate to the account executive and legal. Please share availability for a committee meeting and the raw telemetry by EOD today.

Regards,
Alyssa Turner
SRE, FidelityCloud
alyssa@fidelitycloud.com
